clue.text: Three leaflets on work about umpire

indicators.note: about means going round, so the word for work wraps the umpire's word

parts.note: to toil is to work
a ref, short for referee, is an umpire

explanation.surface: A clover-like plant growing on the cricket field where the umpire works.
explanation.definitionFit: A clover plant or Gothic ornament with three lobes, as the name (Latin for three leaves) says.

clue.text: Finished the tunnel?…

explanation.surface: Someone asks if the tunnel has been completed.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs on to the next clue, whose answer is also a word for finished.
explanation.definitionFit: Being done with something means being finished; a tunnel is a passage that goes right from one side to the other.

clue.text: … just finished!

parts.note: read as a plain past tense, something that has come to a close, carrying on the previous clue's word for done

explanation.surface: An exclamation that the work is complete at last.
explanation.walkthrough: This clue continues 1-down via the ellipsis, giving a second word for finished.
explanation.definitionFit: Simple past tense synonym: something concluded has come to its close.

clue.text: The rector has arranged for a band

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of these two words are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: A clergyman has organised a musical group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' shuffles RECTOR plus HAS; 'The' and 'for a' are linking words. 'arranged' also hints at music, which hides the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A large musical ensemble is a band of players.

clue.text: Retreat to dead end by Scottish proprietor

parts.note: a lair is an animal's den, a retreat

indicators.note: end of the word dead means only its final letter is taken

explanation.surface: A landowner goes back to a dead end.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland a landed estate owner is called by this title.

clue.text: Untwisting threads is most difficult

indicators.note: untwisting the strands of a word suggests its letters come apart and are rearranged

explanation.surface: Unravelling yarn is the toughest job.
explanation.definitionFit: Superlative synonym: the toughest or most difficult.

clue.text: Looking back, animal had a vision

parts.note: a hind is a female deer, an animal
sight means vision

explanation.surface: Gazing behind it, a creature had a revelation.
explanation.definitionFit: Hindsight is understanding gained by reviewing events once they are past.

clue.text: We hear a critique of a musical show

indicators.note: we hear means a word is identified by how it is pronounced when spoken

parts.note: a review is a critique

explanation.surface: Listeners hear a critic's verdict on a musical production.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatrical entertainment of songs and sketches is a revue.

clue.text: Endless stairs caused a lost race

indicators.note: caused means the following letters are made into something new, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A never-ending staircase made people lose a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caused' is the anagram signal working on A LOST RACE; 'lost' belongs to the fodder though it reads like the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A moving staircase whose steps loop round endlessly.

clue.text: One in dealings involving long harangues

indicators.note: in means the letter for one sits inside the word for dealings

parts.note: trades are business dealings
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A businessman's trading leads to lengthy rants.
explanation.definitionFit: Long angry speeches of denunciation are harangues.

clue.text: Introduce changes to bring things down

definitions.note: a verb phrase defining a noun meaning the act of lowering

indicators.note: changes means the letters of the word introduce are rearranged

explanation.surface: Bringing in alterations to lower prices.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut or lowering is the act of making things smaller or less.

clue.text: Minister puts five into first vehicle

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral five
I is the Roman numeral one, first
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A clergyman parks his vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A parish priest in the Church of England is a minister of religion.

clue.text: Bad end of two universities was unnecessary

indicators.note: bad means the letters are spoiled and rearranged

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for university, so two give two Us

explanation.surface: A poor finish for two colleges was uncalled for.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive or uncalled-for means beyond what is needed.

clue.text: Destroyed-finished without charm

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the word for finished goes round the charm

parts.note: died means finished, came to an end
a spell is a magic charm

explanation.surface: Something was wrecked once the magic stopped working.
explanation.definitionFit: Doubts dispelled are driven off and so destroyed.

clue.text: Prevent activity of amateur violinist

parts.note: a ham is an inept amateur performer
a violinist is a string, one of the string section

explanation.surface: An unskilled fiddler stops the performance.
explanation.definitionFit: To cripple someone by cutting the tendon behind the knee, hence to hinder or prevent action.

clue.text: Animals go for these trees

indicators.note: for here signals that the words before are turned into something else, rearranged

explanation.surface: Beasts head off towards these trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is the only word to signal the anagram of ANIMALS GO, a loose signal; 'these' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Flowering trees with large showy blooms.

clue.text: Earliest one, perhaps, of those living in Jerusalem

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: The first inhabitant of Jerusalem, possibly.
explanation.definitionFit: Belonging to the ancient Hebrew people of Israel, whose capital was Jerusalem.

clue.text: Tries out ceremonies

indicators.note: out means the letters of tries are put out of order

explanation.surface: Someone tests out rituals.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal religious acts or ceremonies.

clue.text: About to make a change in style

parts.note: re means about, concerning
fashion means style

explanation.surface: Someone is about to alter their look.
explanation.definitionFit: To give something a new form is to alter or remodel it.

clue.text: Follow some degree of strong opinion

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them
MA is a Master of Arts degree

explanation.surface: Stick to a degree of firm belief.
explanation.definitionFit: A firmly held doctrine or belief laid down as true.

clue.text: Wanted teacher to be involved in the action

indicators.note: to be involved in means the teacher's word goes inside the action word

parts.note: a deed is an action
sir is how British pupils address a male teacher

explanation.surface: A teacher wanted to take part in what was happening.
explanation.definitionFit: Longed for or wished for.

clue.text: Rhode Island floater for tiny aquatic animal

indicators.note: for here signals that the words before are turned into something else, rearranged

parts.note: RI is the US postal abbreviation for Rhode Island

explanation.surface: A drifter from Rhode Island stands in for a small water creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is the only word left to signal the anagram of RI plus FLOATER. The answer is the adjective of rotifer, a microscopic water animal, used loosely as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to rotifers, microscopic many-celled creatures of fresh water.

clue.text: The girl who became slimmer

parts.note: a woman who has lost weight now weighs less on the scales

explanation.surface: A young woman who lost weight.
explanation.definitionFit: Weighing less is being less heavy, the comparative of the word for not heavy.

clue.text: Demonstrate with a bit of a fine specimen

parts.note: to show is to demonstrate
a piece is a bit

explanation.surface: Displaying part of an excellent example.
explanation.definitionFit: An outstanding example displayed for admiration.

clue.text: Father's thanks for the Italian food

parts.note: pa is father, with the 's kept as S
ta is British informal for thanks

explanation.surface: Dad says thank you for the spaghetti.
explanation.definitionFit: Dough of wheat flour shaped into spaghetti, macaroni and so on.

clue.text: Go in from an open terrace

indicators.note: from means the letters are taken from within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Come inside off an exposed patio.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to come or go into a place.

clue.text: Flexible wings cause movement to and fro

indicators.note: flexible means the letters bend into a new order

explanation.surface: Bendy wings make something sway back and forth.
explanation.definitionFit: A swaying back-and-forth motion, like a pendulum's.

clue.text: Terrorists question one from the middle east

parts.note: the IRA, the Irish Republican Army
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Gunmen interrogate a man from the Middle East.
explanation.definitionFit: Belonging to Iraq, a country of the Middle East.

clue.text: Gives assistance right before attacks

indicators.note: before means the letter for right comes ahead of the next piece

parts.note: aids means gives assistance

explanation.surface: Helping out precedes offensive strikes.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudden assaults or forays.

clue.text: Training furiously to a T and arousing curiosity

indicators.note: furiously means the letters of training are thrown wildly about

explanation.surface: Fierce exercise done perfectly makes people curious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to a T' means perfectly, but here simply adds a T after the shuffled TRAINING.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a schemer, someone who arouses interest through plotting; the clue treats it as stirring curiosity.

clue.text: Ailment which can be picked up at the seaside

indicators.note: picked up suggests the letters are collected and put together in a fresh order

explanation.surface: An illness you might catch on a beach holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' reads as catching an illness but signals the shuffle of SEASIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Illness or sickness; an ailment.

clue.text: When one is found in an athlete he's not so stiff

indicators.note: is found in means the letter for one sits inside the athlete word

parts.note: a runner is an athlete
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A sportsman with an extra one becomes less rigid.
explanation.definitionFit: More fluid or liquid, so less stiff.
